paragraphs: R. Neḥemyah, Terumot 8:7; Ma'aserot 3:5; Shabbat 8:4, 17:4; Yevamot 5:6; Nedarim 3:11; Nazir 9:4; Sotah 5:4; Sanhedrin 1:6, 9:1, 10:3; Zevaḥim 13:6; Niddah 9:3; Zavim 4:3, 7; Tevul Yom 3:1; Makhshirin 3:2; Kelim 18:5; Nega'im 11:5; Nedarim 4:3. Whether he is R. Nehorai: see his entry. Bereshit Rabbah, Vayeḥi, section 98, says he descends from Neḥemyah the Tirshata. R. Yehudah ben Bava ordained him (see his entry). The anonymous rulings of the Tosefta are attributed to R. Neḥemyah, following his teacher R. Akiva, Sanhedrin 86. Tosafot Yoma 40b calls him R. Akiva's student; Bereshit Rabbah 61. In his father's name, Pesaḥim 54a. Sifra, Metzora, at 'He shall take one lamb': R. Akiva asked R. Neḥemyah. Nearby: R. Neḥemyah and R. Eliezer ben Yaakov; Zevaḥim 65a; Bava Metzia 62. Seven elders went to intercalate the year: R. Meir, R. Yehudah, R. Yose, R. Shimon, R. Neḥemyah, R. Eliezer ben Yaakov and R. Yoḥanan the Sandalmaker (see his entry). R. Neḥemyah and R. Elazar say, Tosefta Menaḥot 7. In R. Elazar son of R. Yose the Galilean's name, Bereshit Rabbah 26. He disagrees with R. Yehudah, Makkot 11; Middot 11 [source locator]; and with R. Shimon, Eruvin 5. Between R. Yehudah and R. Neḥemyah the law follows R. Neḥemyah, Sefer Keritot, Yemot Olam, gate 3.
